com.naver.linewebtoon.signInSdk: androidx Credential Manager (Play services provider) and Facebook Login

launch.evidence: Splash then the login screen (Continue with Email / Google / Facebook) rendered; the first frame of the login screen appeared only after another event (frame lag).

google_account_selection.evidence: Continue with Google -> Credential Manager found no framework credential service and used Play services (androidx.credentials HiddenActivity -> GIS PendingIntent). 'Choose an account to continue to WEBTOON' listed the test account; selecting it returned RESULT_OK.

google_tokens.evidence: The broker issued two OAuth tokens and an ID token for WEBTOON's server client ID (google_server_app_id) and granted the session.

google_sign_in.gap: After the credential reached the app, WEBTOON showed 'Login with your Google account failed.' WEBTOON made no further Play services call; its own login step (server) refused or failed. Cause open (not observable without the app's network trace).
google_sign_in.rerun: Rerun on 2026-11-21 board time (HKT) with both fixes: same "Login with your Google account failed." after Play services returned RESULT_OK to androidx.credentials HiddenActivity. Not the descriptor bugs; open.
google_sign_in.analysis: WEBTOON's handler for the Credential Manager result (GoogleLoginActivity) parses the Google ID token credential and then calls the Authorization API (Identity.getAuthorizationClient(activity).authorize: email and profile scopes, offline access, the chosen account); the dialog comes from that call's failure listener. Whether the request reaches Play services is not established yet. Play services logged WL-AUTH-PROXY package_accounts count=0 for WEBTOON, but in the same second as the broker issued the picker's tokens, so it belongs to the picker flow.
google_sign_in.cause: Found with WESTLAKE_PLAY_TRACE=1 (2026-11-21 board time): after the ID token reaches WEBTOON, its Authorization API call asks Play services for service 219 and gets status 9 (SERVICE_INVALID). Play services refuses the service to uncertified devices; 219 is not on the approved exception list (212, 213, 91, 44, 5, 29). The sign-in service 212 answered status 0. Uncertified-device policy, not a Westlake gap, unless the user approves adding 219.
google_sign_in.after_219: With 219 added to the eligibility list (363a071, framework v27 on Play services, 2026-11-21 board time): service 219 answers status 0 and WEBTOON calls IAuthorizationService.authorize, which calls back. The login still fails. During the authorize step Play services asked for WEBTOON's accounts twice and got none (WL-AUTH-PROXY package_accounts count=0), and no token request reached the broker. Next gap: the chosen account is visible to an app only while its picker is open or while Play services serves its synchronous call. The asynchronous Authorization API needs the same mediation as the legacy asynchronous sign-in (GoogleAsyncAuthOperations), including the server auth code.

summary.rollout: Runtime cef91a38 runs in Play services, the Store and Gmail (2026-11-21 board time); Duolingo's Google sign-in verified through the restarted Play services.

westlakeFixes.f46ae1b: Window shim: perform(NATIVE_WINDOW_GET_LAST_QUEUED_BUFFER/_2) now writes no buffer and fence -1 before its error. hwui's PixelCopy readback (Readback::copySurfaceInto) closes that fence on every return path, so the unwritten value closed whatever its stack held: another thread's descriptor when that number was open. Root cause of Duolingo's in-app browser aborts ([FATAL:scoped_file.cc(43)] and [FATAL:udp_socket_posix.cc(276)] Bad file descriptor) and of its RenderThread Looper POLL_ERROR. Found with a kernel trace of fd_install and every close with its user-space caller; the fixed run had no descriptor closed by anyone but its owner across about a million traced events.
westlakeFixes.876034c-deployment: The runtime deployed for this stack (8e5d7304) was built from a worktree without westlake 876034c (the input receiver keeps its own duplicate of the channel descriptor), so each window teardown closed one descriptor number twice. Rebuilt byte-for-byte from the recorded command with only that change: cef91a38.
